info.title: NextExplorer API
info.description:
Everything the interface does, it does over this API: there is no reduced
API for automation.

**Signing in.** A script should use an API token, from Settings → API tokens,
in `Authorization: Bearer nxe_…`. A `read` token reaches reads only; no
token reaches the account, administration, the terminal or the editor
integrations. The interface uses a session cookie from `POST /api/auth/login`.
Who may call each operation is in its security requirements and, in words, in
`x-access`.

**Paths.** Files are named by where they are: a volume path
(`Documents/2026/report.pdf`), `personal/…` for the account’s own folder, an
assigned volume’s label, or `share/<token>/…` inside a link.

**Errors** are JSON and carry a `requestId` that also appears in the server
log. **Nothing is ever written over:** a name already taken becomes `name (1)`.

**Not versioned.** This is the interface’s own API and changes with it; an
instance serves the description of its own release at `/api/openapi.json`.

post.summary: Sign in with a password
post.description: Answers the account and sets the session cookie. An account with a second factor answers `{ "totpRequired": true }` instead, and the session holds the sign-in for five minutes until the code arrives.

oneOf.description: The password was right; finish at `POST /api/auth/login/totp`.

post.summary: Finish signing in with a code
post.description: The six digits from the authenticator, or one recovery code. A wrong code counts against the same lockout as a wrong password (`AUTH_INVALID_TOTP_CODE`).

post.summary: Begin signing in with a passkey
post.description: The challenge inside `options` is spent by the matching finish.

post.summary: Sign in with the passkey’s answer
post.description: Every refusal is `401` with `AUTH_PASSKEY_REJECTED`, whatever the reason. A passkey that was not unlocked on an account with a second factor answers `{ "totpRequired": true }`.

oneOf.description: The password was right; finish at `POST /api/auth/login/totp`.

post.summary: Sign out this session
post.description: Ends the application’s session. Signing out at the identity provider as well is `GET /logout`, which a browser navigates to.

provider.description: How this session signed in — `local` or `oidc`. On the signed-in account only.

lockedUntil.description: Set while failed sign-ins keep the account locked.

readOnly.description: Why nothing can be written here when the storage itself refuses it, for everyone: `storage` for a read-only mount, `permission` for a folder the server may not write in. The write permissions above are then all false.

Access.description: What this caller may do here — asked before trying, rather than learned from a refusal.

path.description: The folder it is in, not including its own name.

kind.description: `directory` for a folder, `volume` at the top, otherwise the extension in lower case — `pdf`, `md`, `unknown`.

size.description: Bytes. For a folder, what the file system reports for the folder itself.

supportsThumbnail.description: A thumbnail can be asked for at `/api/thumbnails/…`.

versions.description: Earlier versions kept, where this caller may see them.

onlyofficeActivity.description: Somebody has it open in ONLYOFFICE right now.

code.description: A stable name for the refusal, where there is one — `AUTH_TOKEN_READ_ONLY`, `ARCHIVE_ENCRYPTED`.

requestId.description: Also in the server log: what to quote when something needs explaining.

userIds.description: The accounts it is shared with, when `sharingType` is `users`.

shareUrl.description: Built from `PUBLIC_URL` when it is set. On creation.

modifiedAt.description: When the file had this content.

source.description: What kept it — a save from the editor, an upload over it, an office session.

pinned.description: Kept whatever thinning would otherwise do.

aside.description: Set aside by a co-editor’s save rather than kept on a schedule.

options.description: What `navigator.credentials` expects, every byte as base64url.

dirty.description: Counted before something changed under it.

path.description: Where it is on the server.

E400.description: The request is not one this operation can act on; the message says why.

E401.description: Nobody is signed in, or the credential presented is not usable. The gate in front of every route answers `{ "error" }`; a route answers the usual error body.

E403.description: Signed in, and not allowed — including an API token at a door it never opens.

E404.description: Not there, or not somewhere this caller may see.

E409.description: The state of things does not allow it — a name taken, an archive behind a password.

E415.description: Not a kind of file this operation reads.

E422.description: Understood, and impossible — a damaged archive.

E423.description: Held by something else for the moment.

E429.description: Too many attempts; wait before trying again.

E500.description: Something failed on the server; the request id is in its log.

E502.description: A server this operation relies on — the identity provider — did not answer.

E503.description: A tool this operation needs is not installed on this server, or the feature is off.

session.name: connect.sid
session.description: The session the interface uses, from `POST /api/auth/login`. As wide as the account it belongs to.

apiToken.description: An API token, `nxe_…`, from Settings → API tokens, in the `Authorization` header and nowhere else. A `read` token reaches reads only (and `POST /api/download`); no token reaches the account, administration, the terminal or an editor integration.

guestSession.name: X-Guest-Session
guestSession.description: What opening a shared link earns, from `POST /api/share/{token}/verify` or `GET /api/share/{token}/access`. Also accepted as the `guestSession` cookie.
